meta.title: Lifetime months ≈ 1 / monthly churn
meta.summary: SAMPLE 5% monthly churn → ~20 months. Do not mix monthly with annual churn.

success.message:
Session complete. Churn = lost ÷ customers at the start. Lifetime months ≈ 1 ÷ monthly churn. Name the period.

SAMPLE: 24 ÷ 800 = 3%; 5% → ~20 months, 2% → ~50.

start.message: SAMPLE: 5% monthly churn. How long do they stay, roughly?

wrong_start_times.message:
You annualized the percent as if it were years of life. Inverse the monthly rate.

Return to 1/churn.

wrong_start_retention.message:
That is the retention percent, not a lifetime. Invert the churn: 1 ÷ 0.05 = 20.

Return to 1/churn.

base.message:
You started the month with 800 customers, signed 200, and lost 24.

Monthly churn?

wrong_base_with_new.message:
New signups had no chance to churn yet. Divide by the start: 800 → 3%.

Revisit the denominator.

wrong_base_end.message:
Divide by customers at the start of the month: 3%.

Revisit the denominator.

mix.message:
Someone quotes 5% churn without saying monthly vs yearly.

What do you do?

choices.label: Ask the period before inverting — 5% yearly is ~20 years, not 20 months

wrong_mix_assume_m.message:
Founders mix periods. 5% yearly inverted is decades. Ask.

Revisit the period.

wrong_mix_assume_y.message:
SaaS often means monthly. The skill is to notice the missing unit.

Revisit the period.

wrong_check_24.message:
That mixes percent and months. Inverse the rate.

Try the check again.
